newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti says jobs question resolved.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti says jobs question resolved.

text.p: The leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation, Fausto Bertinotti, said on Thursday that his differences with Italy's centre-left government over employment policy had been resolved.
"The stalemate and division that had arisen within the (governing) majority has been unblocked," Bertinotti said in statement.
Earlier Bertinotti met for four hours with the leaders of coalition parties to discuss the issue which had created deep tensions within Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government.
"The problem of employment is so dramatic that we need to do something good immediately. This we can now do," Bertinotti said in his statement.
He said the government would introduce measures guaranteeing 100,000 new jobs for unemployed youths in the depressed south of the country.
However he indicated that the government planned to press ahead with plans to introduce incentives to encourage short-term contracts, which his party still opposed.
"But we need to underline that a step forward has been made," the statement said.

Refoundation had threatened to vote against a bill on employment which is currently going before parliament. The government is expected to introduce the amendments agreed with the hard-left party next week. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
